licence.notes: 文章为基于公开新闻事实的原创改写，不含源文连续原文，URL 仅作事实溯源。事实归属：英格兰与威尔士 2026 年 5-6 月热浪死亡估算（伦敦卫生与热带医学院 / 帝国理工 / 英国气象局，逾 2700 例、5 月约 550、6 月约 2200、归因占比 42%、5 月 59%、6 月 38%、日最高温 +3–4 °C、东南 549/伦敦 453/西米德兰兹 368、6 月每百万人 49 例、85 岁以上约 60%）；湿球温度 35 °C 上限（Sherwood 与 Huber，PNAS 2010）与 HEAT-Lim 模型（Vanos 等，2023；Perkins-Kirkpatrick 与 Jay 等，Nature Communications 2026，六场历史热浪、凤凰城 24%、马里科帕县 645 例、室内死亡 156 例中 95%）；劳动损失（ILO 2026 年 4 月报告 24.1 亿劳动者、占比 71%、2030 年 2.2% 工时 / 8000 万岗位 / 2.4 万亿美元；WHO 2285 万例工伤、WBGT 每升 1 °C 降 2–3%；英国 6 月下旬 2400 万工时 / 15.5 亿美元）；巴塞罗那降温模拟（ICTA-UAB，Sergi Ventura，白屋顶 1.75 °C、公园 0.26 °C、绿化屋顶 0.37 °C、夜间升温、2100 年效果降至 16%）；博帕尔 Smart Surfaces（TERI / Smart Surfaces Coalition / 麦克阿瑟基金会，2026 年 6 月 5 日，463 平方公里、平均反照率 0.165、降温 3 °C、十年 3.5 倍回报）；IEA 2050 年 10 亿台空调；WHO 欧洲区 2026 年第二版热健康行动计划指南八要素；凤凰城、迈阿密-戴德县热官。

source.derivation: 基于公开新闻事实由模型改写成雅思学术体并命题 信源: https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/about-us/news-and-media/media-centre/weather-and-climate-news/2026/more-than-2700-excess-deaths-estimated-in-england-and-wales-during-may-and-june-heatwaves | https://www.lshtm.ac.uk/newsevents/news/2026/more-2700-excess-deaths-estimated-england-and-wales-during-may-and-june | https://www.chinadailyhk.com/hk/article/636343 | https://spacedaily.com/n-for-more-than-a-decade-the-benchmark-for-human-heat-survival-has-been-a-wet-bulb-temperature-of-35-degrees-celsius-sustained-for-six-hours-a-number-researchers-have-now-found-is-far-higher | https://www.emjreviews.com/general-healthcare/news/deadly-heat-stress-thresholds-cooler-than-previously-thought/ | https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/1132533 | https://teriin.org/press-release/bhopal-one-hottest-cities-india-could-cool-itself-3degc-citywide-smart-surfaces | https://wageindicator.org/what-we-do/news-stories/work-extreme-heat | https://www.weforum.org/stories/nature-and-biodiversity/europe-heatwaves-wildfires-charts/ | https://www.who.int/europe/activities/planning-heat-health-action | https://climatecompass247.com/climate/11-cities-exploring-new-ways-to-protect-residents-from-extreme-heat/

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Britain's summer of 2026 arrived early. Two heatwaves struck England and Wales in May and June, both breaking long-standing records. A rapid assessment by researchers at the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, Imperial College London and the Met Office estimated that heat caused more than 2,700 excess deaths: approximately 550 between 21 and 29 May and roughly 2,200 between 18 and 28 June. Around 42 per cent of these deaths were attributed to the extra warmth generated by human activity, which lifted daytime maxima by 3–4 °C; the attributable share was higher in May, at 59 per cent, than in June, at 38 per cent.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The burden was unevenly distributed. Across both events the South East of England recorded the highest estimated number of excess deaths, at 549, followed by London with 453 and the West Midlands with 368. Adjusted for population, however, the West Midlands had the highest rate in June, at 49 deaths per million residents, a pattern the researchers read as evidence that populations rarely exposed to extreme heat are less prepared for it. Age was the strongest predictor of risk: people aged over 85 accounted for some 60 per cent of all excess deaths.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Judgements about heat risk long rested on one number. In 2010 Steven Sherwood and Matthew Huber argued in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences that a wet-bulb temperature of 35 °C, which combines heat with humidity, is the point where sweat can no longer evaporate fast enough to hold the core temperature near 37 °C. Sustained for six hours, they calculated, it would kill even a fit adult at rest. The value was meant as an absolute ceiling, not a comfort guide, but became a standard marker of lethality. A study published in Nature Communications in March 2026, led by Sarah Perkins-Kirkpatrick and including Ollie Jay, applied a physiological model, HEAT-Lim, developed in 2023 by Jennifer Vanos and colleagues, and concluded that the ceiling is too high.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The newer model adds variables the older one ignored: age, direct sunlight and the lower sweating capacity of older bodies. Applied to six historical heatwaves in Mecca, Bangkok, Phoenix, Mount Isa, Larkana and Seville, none of which had sustained 35 °C, it found that all six had crossed HEAT-Lim's threshold of non-survivability for people over 65 in direct sun. In Phoenix in July 2023, 24 per cent of rolling six-hour periods breached it, and Maricopa County recorded 645 heat-related deaths that summer, almost two-thirds among people aged 50 or above. Of the 156 deaths that occurred indoors, 95 per cent were in the same age group. Hot but dry conditions proved as dangerous as humid ones.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Heat also carries a large economic cost. A report published by the International Labour Organization in April 2026 estimated that 2.41 billion workers, around 71 per cent of the global workforce, are exposed to excessive heat each year, and that the World Health Organization attributes more than 22.85 million occupational injuries annually to such exposure. Productivity falls by roughly 2–3 per cent for each degree by which the wet-bulb globe temperature exceeds 20 °C. By 2030, the ILO projects, heat stress could remove 2.2 per cent of total working hours worldwide, the equivalent of 80 million full-time jobs and $2.4 trillion of output.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Cities have begun to experiment with surfaces. A team led by Sergi Ventura at the Institute of Environmental Science and Technology of the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona simulated future heatwaves across the Barcelona metropolitan area and compared three strategies. White roofs performed best during daylight, reducing temperatures by up to 1.75 °C in the most vulnerable districts, though the researchers warned that reflective coatings on façades could raise street-level temperatures instead. New parks and peri-urban farmland produced moderate daytime cooling of 0.26 °C, and irrigated green roofs 0.37 °C, but both vegetation-based measures raised night-time temperatures slightly. Ventura explained that vegetation releases at night the heat stored by day, limiting radiative cooling.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Whether such measures work across a whole city was examined in Bhopal, India, where The Energy and Resources Institute and the Smart Surfaces Coalition modelled a decade of interventions for the municipal corporation, supported by the MacArthur Foundation. The analysis mapped reflectivity across 463 square kilometres and found an average albedo of just 0.165, meaning most surfaces absorb about 83 per cent of the sunlight reaching them. Full adoption of reflective roofs and pavements, rooftop solar panels and additional tree cover was projected to cut peak summer temperatures by up to 3 °C, returning 3.5 times its cost over a decade. Low-income districts, typically 5–6 °C hotter than wealthier ones, were expected to gain most.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Sceptics point to how quickly such returns diminish. The Barcelona team calculated that their strategies could cut heat vulnerability by 43–47 per cent under present conditions, but by only about 16 per cent under warming projected for 2100, and that vulnerability in dense, low-income districts could double. Mechanical cooling offers no straightforward escape: the International Energy Agency expects the global stock of air conditioners to reach one billion units by 2050, yet they expel waste heat outdoors and can raise city temperatures by around 2 °C. Attention has consequently turned to governance: in 2026 the World Health Organization's European office published a second edition of its heat-health action plan guidance, and cities including Phoenix have appointed heat officers.

question_groups.instruction: The reading passage has eight paragraphs, A–H. Choose the correct heading for each paragraph from the list of headings below.

options.text: The demographic and regional pattern of heat-related deaths
Reassessing a long-standing measure of survivable heat
Evidence that lethal thresholds have already been crossed
The economic cost to workers and employers
Comparing the cooling performance of different urban surfaces
A city-wide plan and its projected returns
Why adaptation alone will not be enough
Estimating the mortality of an unprecedented summer

evidence.quote: Age was the strongest predictor of risk: people aged over 85 accounted for some 60 per cent of all excess deaths.

paraphrase.to: Age was the strongest predictor of risk / unevenly distributed

questions.explanation: B 段主旨不是估算死亡总数（那是 A 段），而是死亡负担在地区和年龄上的分布：东南区最多、西米德兰兹按人口计最高、85 岁以上占六成。

evidence.quote: A study published in Nature Communications in March 2026, led by Sarah Perkins-Kirkpatrick and including Ollie Jay, applied a physiological model, HEAT-Lim, developed in 2023 by Jennifer Vanos and colleagues, and concluded that the ceiling is too high.

paraphrase.to: concluded that the ceiling is too high

questions.explanation: C 段先交代沿用十余年的 35 °C 湿球温度上限，再讲 2026 年研究用 HEAT-Lim 重新评估、认为该上限定得过高。注意与 iii 的区别：列举六场热浪的实证在 D 段。

evidence.quote: Applied to six historical heatwaves in Mecca, Bangkok, Phoenix, Mount Isa, Larkana and Seville, none of which had sustained 35 °C, it found that all six had crossed HEAT-Lim's threshold of non-survivability for people over 65 in direct sun.

paraphrase.from: Evidence that lethal thresholds have already been crossed
paraphrase.to: all six had crossed HEAT-Lim's threshold of non-survivability

questions.explanation: D 段用六场历史热浪的实测数据说明：即使从未达到 35 °C，致命阈值也已被突破。

evidence.quote: A team led by Sergi Ventura at the Institute of Environmental Science and Technology of the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona simulated future heatwaves across the Barcelona metropolitan area and compared three strategies.

questions.explanation: F 段逐项比较白屋顶、绿化屋顶和城市公园三类降温手段的效果。vi（全市方案与收益）对应的是 G 段博帕尔，不是 F 段。

evidence.quote: The Barcelona team calculated that their strategies could cut heat vulnerability by 43–47 per cent under present conditions, but by only about 16 per cent under warming projected for 2100, and that vulnerability in dense, low-income districts could double.

paraphrase.from: Why adaptation alone will not be enough
paraphrase.to: returns diminish / Mechanical cooling offers no straightforward escape

questions.explanation: H 段核心是适应措施的收益随升温急剧衰减、空调并非出路，最后转向治理手段，即「单靠适应不够」。

question_groups.instruction: Do the following statements agree with the information given in the reading passage?

questions.stem: A greater share of the deaths in the May heatwave than in the June heatwave was put down to human-induced warming.

evidence.quote: the attributable share was higher in May, at 59 per cent, than in June, at 38 per cent

paraphrase.from: was put down to human-induced warming
paraphrase.to: attributed ... to the extra warmth generated by human activity

questions.explanation: A 段末句明确：5 月可归因比例为 59%，6 月为 38%，故 5 月更高。

questions.stem: HEAT-Lim was devised by the authors of the 2026 Nature Communications study.

evidence.quote: A study published in Nature Communications in March 2026, led by Sarah Perkins-Kirkpatrick and including Ollie Jay, applied a physiological model, HEAT-Lim, developed in 2023 by Jennifer Vanos and colleagues, and concluded that the ceiling is too high.

paraphrase.from: was devised by the authors of the 2026 study
paraphrase.to: developed in 2023 by Jennifer Vanos and colleagues

questions.explanation: C 段说 HEAT-Lim 由 Jennifer Vanos 及其同事于 2023 年开发，2026 年论文的作者只是「应用」它，不是「开发」它。题干张冠李戴，故 FALSE。

questions.stem: In Barcelona, green roofs were found to make night-time temperatures slightly higher.

evidence.quote: New parks and peri-urban farmland produced moderate daytime cooling of 0.26 °C, and irrigated green roofs 0.37 °C, but both vegetation-based measures raised night-time temperatures slightly.

questions.explanation: F 段说两类植被措施（含绿化屋顶）都使夜间温度略微上升，题干与原文一致。

questions.stem: The International Labour Organization's 2026 report recommends a legal maximum temperature for outdoor workplaces.

evidence.quote: A report published by the International Labour Organization in April 2026 estimated that 2.41 billion workers, around 71 per cent of the global workforce, are exposed to excessive heat each year

questions.explanation: E 段只讲 ILO 对暴露人数、工伤数量和工时损失的估算，全文没有任何关于「法定最高工作温度」的立法建议（H 段提到的是 WHO 的行动指南与城市热官），属未提及。

question_groups.instruction: Answer the questions below. Choose NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER from the passage for each answer. (Question 13: NO MORE THAN FOUR WORDS.)

questions.stem: In which part of England was the largest number of excess heat-related deaths across the two 2026 heatwaves estimated?

evidence.quote: Across both events the South East of England recorded the highest estimated number of excess deaths, at 549, followed by London with 453 and the West Midlands with 368.

questions.explanation: B 段首句：东南英格兰 549 例最多，伦敦 453、西米德兰兹 368。注意题干问绝对数，不是按人口计的比率。

questions.stem: What percentage of the heat-related deaths that occurred indoors in Maricopa County involved people aged 50 or over?

evidence.quote: Of the 156 deaths that occurred indoors, 95 per cent were in the same age group.

questions.explanation: D 段：156 例室内死亡中 95% 属于同一年龄段，即上一句所说的 50 岁及以上人群。

questions.stem: According to the International Labour Organization, how many workers are exposed to excessive heat each year?

evidence.quote: A report published by the International Labour Organization in April 2026 estimated that 2.41 billion workers, around 71 per cent of the global workforce, are exposed to excessive heat each year

paraphrase.from: According to the International Labour Organization
paraphrase.to: A report published by the International Labour Organization

questions.explanation: E 段首句，ILO 2026 年 4 月报告估计 24.1 亿劳动者每年暴露于过度高温。

questions.stem: Which organisation forecasts that the global number of air-conditioning units will reach one billion by 2050?

evidence.quote: the International Energy Agency expects the global stock of air conditioners to reach one billion units by 2050

paraphrase.to: the global stock of air conditioners

questions.explanation: H 段：国际能源署预计全球空调存量到 2050 年将达 10 亿台。注意不要与同段WHO 欧洲区办公室混淆。
